findings.text: the a-refusal-is-about-the-work §3 row cites `reckon/crew/runs.py:2160` for `follower_state` and `runs.py:2170` for `list_followers`, but at base 9945557624511d329211b5b573cdf77d38b02ac4 line 2160 is `if not directory.is_dir():` inside list_followers and line 2170 is a comment about released registrations, while the symbols are at 2146 and 2157; these are the row's own deduplication premise (the released-versus-never distinction that `_follower_liveness` already computes), so the drift is 13 to 14 lines rather than the one- and two-line slips elsewhere and both citations send a reader to code that is not the named reuse target.

the a-worker-can-take-a-brief §2 row's TaskNode sub-citations (`plan` 590, `section` 591, `as_dict` 602) are all off at the stated base: `reckon/crew/node.py:590` is `goal: str`, 591 is `plan: str`, 592 is `section` and `as_dict` is at 604, so each of the three pointers names the neighbouring field and the carrier the row tells the implementer to widen is misdescribed at every one of them.

item_verdicts.diff: there is no diff, because the node landed no commit and its only deliverable path is outside every repository, so I read the artifact against the base tree instead: reuse-map.md:15-18 is the whole change, and I re-derived its substantive claims at 9945557624511d329211b5b573cdf77d38b02ac4 and found them true, namely both absence claims re-run with positive controls (--brief 0 vs --plan 6 hits, evidence/fragments 0 vs evidence/archive 31 hits), require_plan_section_visible resolving to one call site at reckon/crew/dispatch.py:3102, the six watch_state sites with reckon/crew/dispatch.py:4493 inside dispatch(), the four plan-section quotations matching the plan HTML verbatim, and every named test file and path existing at the base.
item_verdicts.done_when: the evidence fence (prompt.txt:59-63) asks for one row per named section whose entries are each cited as file:line at the dispatch base with a fitness verdict, the four columns, and a manifest naming the base sha and the row count; the map names base 9945557624511d329211b5b573cdf77d38b02ac4 on reuse-map.md:3, the manifest names the same sha and 4 rows, and my independent re-resolution of 63 of its cited lines at that revision found 51 exact, 8 one to two lines off, 2 spanning citations that contain their target and 2 landing on unrelated code (see FINDING), so the shape is fully met while the citation contract itself holds for 81% of the sample.
item_verdicts.goal: the reviewed node's goal (prompt.txt:26) is to map the reuse candidates for the dispatch-surface sections of the S25 first wave, and reuse-map.md:15-18 carries exactly one row for each of the four sections the fence names with all four columns (a)-(d) filled in every row, so the deliverable the goal states is present and complete in substance.
item_verdicts.manifest: read in full; it reads status complete, names base sha 9945557624511d329211b5b573cdf77d38b02ac4 and the 4-row count, and records the eight source-verification commands with their results (the --brief and evidence/fragments greps at 0 hits, the single committed-section call site, the six watch_state sites); two soft spots, both inside the node's declared fence: test_logs names the deliverable reuse-map.md rather than a gate log, and the follow_ons honestly flag the two refused brief strings a-refusal-is-about-the-work §2 must copy as not located rather than guessed.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the manifest declares the single write path the fence grants, the report outside any repository, and that report is the only file the run wrote; the reviewed worktree is clean at 9945557624511d329211b5b573cdf77d38b02ac4 with no commits, which is the correct state for a read-only investigate node whose deliverable lives in the crew reports store rather than in the tree.

justifications.durability: reuse-map.md:3 pins the base revision and the manifest records the method with its commands, but nothing in the artifact fails when a citation drifts, which is the defect this review found only by re-resolving all 63 lines against the base.
justifications.evidence: every substantive claim I re-derived at 9945557624511d329211b5b573cdf77d38b02ac4 holds, including the two absences with their positive controls and the plan quotations, but 2 of 63 sampled citations land on unrelated code and 8 more sit one to two lines off, so the artifact's evidence is verifiable yet not reliably verifiable at its own cited lines (review-citation-check.log).
justifications.fit: reuse-map.md:13-18 follows the form its fence named, with mechanism-named content, no attribution and no plan or ticket identifier in any path, the one point off being that a table-heavy document is markdown where the repository's HTML-first convention would make it a plan document.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reuse-map.md:15-18 answers the goal for all four sections, and the only deduction is that column (a), whose contract is an exact file:line, carries the citation drift the two FINDINGs name.
justifications.scope_discipline: the run wrote exactly its one fenced path and nothing else, the reviewed worktree is clean at the base with changed_paths: [] and no commits, and neither the plan, the project index nor any other repository file was touched.
